page: Google Cloud Platform c3-standard-22 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the c3 server family. It features 22 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 11 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8481C processor running at 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 88.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPU accelerators, and it is provisioned with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The processor features advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for deep learning and matrix operations.

Benchmark evaluations place the c3-standard-22 consistently in the average performance tier across most compute and memory workloads. It achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1715.0 and a multi-core score of 12159.0, alongside a Passmark CPU score of 27864.91. Memory performance is characterized by a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 1497.36 GB/sec and a large block uncached write bandwidth of 46.35 GB/sec. Notably, the server demonstrates strong performance in LLM inference text generation using a small 135M model, reaching 296.59 tokens/sec, while prompt processing for the same model averages 1520.89 tokens/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c3-standard-22 offers a balanced allocation of dedicated compute resources and memory without the added cost of bundled local storage or specialized GPU hardware. This makes it a resource-dense option for workloads that do not require local NVMe drives. The instance is well-suited for general-purpose workloads, software compilation (scoring 19762.0 on Geekbench compiling), database operations (scoring 9968.05 on Passmark database), static web serving (achieving 30.99 GB/sec throughput), and moderate-scale LLM inference tasks.
